### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **`[^R]` marker, p.32**: A footnote marker `[^R]` appears in the table but **the corresponding footnote definition text is NOT present in this section capture**. Per the no-fabrication rule, I will not guess its content. It most likely defines the cash-flow bridge (e.g. "including discontinued operations," "pre-IFRS 16," or a reconciliation note), but this must be verified. → New question Q267.
- **"including discontinued operations" (slide title), p.32**: This is the single most consequential qualification. It means the p.32 waterfall is **group-wide**, not continuing-ops. Any analyst reconciling p.32 to p.31 (continuing-ops FCF) or to the p.27 balance sheet (which reclassifies UK/Poland/Switzerland to held-for-sale) will get a mismatch unless discontinued-ops cash flows are isolated. This directly affects the net-debt reconciliation (Q207/Q223) and the true free-cash figure (Q259).
- **"Cash has been absorbed into operations mainly working capital for H1" (commentary), p.32**: Management attributes the cash absorption to working capital. But the bridge shows NWC only −R369m while **acquisitions/disposals −R778m** and **net finance costs −R397m** are larger drags, and the "cash available to service debt −R1,231m" line is the dominant outflow. The commentary **understates** the non-working-capital drivers (M&A/disposals, finance costs, tax). This is a narrative-vs-numbers tension worth flagging.
- **Column alignment / OCR integrity, p.32**: The table is captured with severe column misalignment (values appear in scattered cells; row labels are jumbled at the bottom). Several signs are unverified (lease +R840m, debt repayments +R585m, other cash +R585m). **The bridge does not arithmetically foot** on the captured numbers. This is a capture-quality qualification, not a company one — but it means every p.32 figure must be re-verified against the printed slide before use in the model.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **No footnote markers (`[^1]`, `*`, etc.) are visible on p.33.** The slide is a pure capex infographic with three bullet callouts. No small-print definitions captured. This is itself a verification point: the "c.1% of revenue" target and the "retailer capital contributions" offset are stated without a footnote defining the revenue base or the gross-vs-net capex convention — both must be checked in the cash-flow/capex note.

- **Qualification 1 — "Capex target of c.1% of revenue remains in place"** `[unmapped, p. 33]`.
  - Implication: This is a **policy/guidance statement**, not a hard number. It implies H2 capex ≈ 1% × H2 revenue. But the revenue base is ambiguous: group revenue R67,482.5m (continuing ops) vs group incl. discontinued. At 1% of R67.5bn ≈ **R675m annual**, i.e. ~R337m per half — yet H1 gross capex was **R659m**, roughly double the run-rate implied by the target. This is a **material tension**: either the target is measured on a net (post-retailer-contribution) basis, or on a full-year basis with H1 front-loading, or the target is being missed. Must be verified against the cash-flow note and any H2 guidance.
  - Forecast impact: If the 1% target binds on gross capex, H2 capex would need to be very low (~R15m) to hit ~R675m FY — implausible. More likely the target is **net capex** (R438.7m H1 → ~R675m FY implies H2 net capex ~R236m). This distinction directly drives FCF and net-debt forecasts.

- **Qualification 2 — "H1 spend on strategic initiatives related to SAP and Omni initiatives"** `[unmapped, p. 33]`.
  - Implication: **Strategic capex = 29% of R659m ≈ R191m** (group). This is largely **IT/intangible-type spend** (SAP finance go-live, Omni). Two issues: (a) is SAP spend capitalised or expensed (opex vs capex classification materially changes EBITDA and FCF)? (b) "SAP finance go-live" in H2 implies **H2 strategic capex skew** and possible **one-off implementation/opex costs** not yet quantified. Must check the intangible-asset note and any H2 guidance.

- **Qualification 3 — "Expansion capex — store acquisition spend of R118m"** `[unmapped, p. 33]`.
  - Implication: R118m of the 30% Expansion bucket (≈R198m) is **store acquisitions**, i.e. inorganic. This ties to Q234/Q266 (acquisitions R214.3m). It means **organic expansion capex is only ~R80m**, which matters for like-for-like new-store contribution and for separating maintenance vs growth capex in the FCF forecast.

- **Qualification 4 — "Replacement capex — Retailer capital contributions of EUR3.8m for store revamps"** `[unmapped, p. 33]`.
  - Implication: This is the **only quantification of the retailer-contribution offset** on the slide. EUR3.8m ≈ **R75m** (at ~19.68 ZAR/EUR closing, p.27) — a partial bridge from R659m gross to R438.7m net (gap ~R220m). The remaining ~R145m of the gross-to-net gap is unexplained here (disposals, timing, other contributions) — must be reconciled in the cash-flow note (Q226/Q263).

- **Qualification 5 — Ireland column: €15m, split 6% / 13% / 81%** `[unmapped, p. 33]`.
  - Implication: Ireland capex is **overwhelmingly Strategic (81% ≈ €12.2m)** vs group 29%. This is a **materially different capex mix** and suggests Ireland H1 spend is front-loaded into strategic/IT projects — relevant to Ireland EBITDA/leverage (3.29x vs 3.50x covenant, p.28) and to whether Ireland capex normalises in H2.

- **Arithmetic checks on the slide:**
  - Group: 30% + 41% + 29% = **100%** ✓ (R659m base).
  - Ireland: 6% + 13% + 81% = **100%** ✓ (€15m base).
  - **Tension flagged**: H1 gross capex R659m vs "c.1% of revenue" target — see Qualification 1. This is a **new verification question** (below).

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **No footnote markers (`[^1]`, `*`, note references) are visible in the captured p. 37 evidence.** The slide is a three-column mitigation framework (Contractual Surcharge Pass-Through / 3PL Renegotiation – Group Scale / Operational Efficiency) with numbered callouts 1–2–3. No small-print definitions, no quantified H2 headwind size, and no footnote text are present in this capture. **Verification question raised**: confirm whether the printed p. 37 slide carries small-print definitions (e.g., "H2 headwind sized" — sized at what amount? "cost per case target" — target level? "delivery savings" — quantum?) that were omitted from this area capture; re-capture full slide body verbatim.

- **Qualification unpacking — "H1 tailwind | H2 headwind sized and mitigated"**: This is a forward-looking claim that H2 fuel/logistics cost pressure is *quantified and offset*. The slide provides mitigation *mechanisms* but **no size of the H2 headwind, no split of how much is mitigated by each lever, and no residual unmitigated cost**. For forecasting, this means H2 W&D cost cannot be modelled from this slide alone; the "sized" claim must be tested against the H2 guidance/outlook section and the fuel/W&D note. Flag as a verification item.

- **Qualification unpacking — "Contractual Surcharge Pass-Through"**: Implies fuel cost increases are contractually recoverable via surcharge and retail price adjustment protocol "under review." Two implications: (i) if pass-through is contractual, H2 fuel inflation should be largely gross-margin/price-neutral at group level, but **the "protocol under review" wording signals the pass-through is not yet locked** — a margin risk if suppliers/retailers resist. (ii) Retail price adjustment affects *revenue* (price inflation) as well as margin — must be separated from volume in the revenue decomposition. Verification: locate the surcharge mechanism terms and whether pass-through is recognised in revenue or as a cost offset.

- **Qualification unpacking — "3PL Renegotiation – Group Scale"**: "SA + Ireland combined logistics volume leveraged in carrier negotiations" implies a *group-level* procurement benefit that may not be visible in SA-only or Ireland-only segment margins. "KZN: structural shift from spot truck hire to owned fleet — cost certainty restored" implies a **capex-for-opex trade**: owned fleet adds depreciation/capex (PP&E) and reduces 3PL hire opex — this must be reflected in the capex forecast and in the W&D cost line, and could flatter H2 opex at the expense of higher D&A. "Ireland: H2 headwind contained; delivery savings partially offsetting" — "partially offsetting" is a qualification that the Ireland headwind is **not fully mitigated**; quantify residual.

- **Qualification unpacking — "Operational Efficiency"**: "Route optimisation & load consolidation — litres consumed down 3.5% in H1" is an *achieved* H1 outcome, not an H2 commitment. "Cost per case target: H2 ambition in place" — "ambition" (not "committed target") is soft forward language; treat as upside risk, not base case. "Cases per man-hour productivity programme — targets reset across all DCs" implies labour cost savings but no quantum. "Fleet additions in KZN" ties to capex (see above).

- **Net effect on forecast**: p. 37 is a *qualitative mitigation framework*, not a quantified bridge. It supports a base-case assumption that H2 W&D cost inflation is partially offset, but the size, split, and residual are not disclosed here and must be sourced from the H2 outlook/guidance section and the W&D/fuel note. The owned-fleet shift and fleet additions create a capex/D&A vs opex substitution that must be modelled explicitly.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **No footnote markers, table notes, or small-print qualifications are visible in the captured evidence for this slide** `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 38]`. The slide is a three-panel macro-outlook graphic ("Constrained Macro environment") with three columns: **Fuel increases**, **Competitive environment**, and **Interest rate hikes expected**. There are no `[^1]`, `*`, or note references to unpack. This is itself a qualification gap: the slide makes forward-looking cost claims ("Successive fuel hikes in H2 to raise distribution and logistics costs"; "Fuel cost increases forecast to impact costs in H2") with **no quantification, no hedging disclosure, and no footnote defining "H2" period, fuel basis, or pass-through mechanism**. A verification question is raised below (Q308) to check whether the printed slide carries small-print not captured.

- **"Constrained Macro environment" heading** `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 38]`: This is a forward-looking framing that qualifies all three panels as *H2 headwinds*, not H1 actuals. It changes the forecast read: the H1 FY2026 results (already reported) should not be extrapolated at H1 run-rate into H2 without overlaying (i) successive SA fuel hikes, (ii) ECB +50bps, (iii) SARB +25bps, and (iv) intensifying discount-format competition / supplier inflation. Each is a margin and/or cost pressure on H2.

- **Fuel increases panel** `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 38]`:
  - SA: "As a result of Middle East conflict — Successive fuel hikes in H2 to raise distribution and logistics costs." This is a **geopolitical supply-shock** driver, not a demand driver. It directly pressures the W&D cost line (R1,709.2m H1, per p. 36) and the fuel line (R254.6m H1, per p. 36). It also interacts with the p. 37 mitigation levers (contractual surcharge pass-through, 3PL renegotiation, owned-fleet shift in KZN, cases-per-man-hour productivity). The slide does **not** quantify the hikes, the pass-through, or the residual — so the "sized and mitigated" claim from p. 37 remains unverified numerically.
  - Ireland: "Fuel cost increases forecast to impact costs in H2." Same directional pressure on Ireland logistics; no quantum.

- **Competitive environment panel** `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 38]`:
  - SA: "Intensifying price competition in SA grocery as chains expand discount formats; Independent retailers under margin pressure." This is a **gross margin and volume** risk, not just a cost risk. It qualifies the p. 37 "retail price adjustment protocol under review" — i.e., the ability to pass through supplier inflation and fuel surcharges is constrained by discount-format competition. It also bears on retailer loyalty/attrition (the 78.5% SA G&L loyalty metric, 77.90% ex-KZN) and on the independent-retailer model that underpins the wholesale revenue base. No quantification.
  - Ireland: "Ireland convenience market remains highly contested." Same directional margin/volume risk for Ireland.

- **Interest rate hikes panel** `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 38]`:
  - SA: "SARB increased interest by 25bps in May 2026." This is a **post-balance-sheet (27 Mar 2026) event** — it does not affect H1 FY2026 net finance cost but is a direct H2 headwind. It bears on the SA leverage/interest-cover covenants (SA 2.73x leverage; 3.25x interest cover per p. 28) and on the R800m hedged at 7.35% (p. 28) — the unhedged portion re-prices.
  - Ireland: "ECB expected to increase interest by at least 50bps in 2026." This **contradicts** the p. 28 commentary that Ireland funding cost is "reducing in line with lower interest rates" — that was an H1 statement; forward guidance is now up. It tightens the already-thin Ireland leverage headroom (3.29x vs 3.50x covenant, p. 28) and Ireland interest cover (4.00x covenant, p. 28).
  - **"Inflation — Increases coming through from suppliers"** is placed under the interest-rate column but is a separate driver: supplier inflation is a COGS/GP% pressure that compounds the fuel and competitive pressures.

- **Net forecast implication of the slide**: H2 FY2026 should be modelled with (a) rising SA and Ireland fuel/logistics costs, (b) constrained pass-through due to discount-format competition, (c) +25bps SA and +50bps ECB interest cost, and (d) supplier inflation. None of these are quantified on the slide — all require the underlying notes (fuel/logistics note, debt note, gross margin note) to size.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **No footnote markers on p. 41.** The slide carries no `[^1]`, `*`, or other footnote markers anywhere in the captured evidence `[unmapped, p. 41]`. This is itself a qualification: several forward-looking claims are **unquantified and undefined**:
  - "Revenue growth accelerated to +2.1% in Feb–Mar" — no base, no LFL vs total, no footnote defining the period or comparator.
  - "GP stabilising" / "GP% recovered from Dec/Jan to March" — no numeric GP%, no definition of "recovered" (to what level?).
  - "Operating profit positive in the final three months of H1" — no Rm figure, no confirmation of group vs SA-only, no footnote on IFRS 16 treatment.
  - "Underlying category mix improving" — "underlying" is undefined; no footnote on what is excluded (e.g., BF promotional distortion, KZN).
  - "Retailer profitability adopted as the primary operating metric" — a **new KPI disclosure** with no definition, no target, no historical series. This is material for forecasting because it signals a shift in management focus from loyalty % to retailer P&L, which may change promotional/subsidy behaviour.
  - "Post-period: early signs of progress albeit y-o-y growth rate impacted by Easter timing" — Easter timing is a **one-off calendar shift** that must be stripped out of H2 run-rate; no quantification given.
  - "APA signed with AF Blakemore (4 May 2026). Saltash Depot and 71 stores" — **post-balance-sheet event**; confirms UK disposal timing (H2 FY2026) and that UK remains in the 27 Mar 2026 balance sheet as held-for-sale/discontinued. No consideration, gain/loss, or lease derecognition amount disclosed.
  - "Final step in the three-year portfolio simplification programme — focus is now entirely on SA and Ireland" — confirms perimeter going forward is **SA + Ireland only**; any residual UK/Poland/Switzerland costs should be treated as non-recurring, but the slide does not quantify residual costs.

- **Qualification implication for forecast**: The slide is a **narrative/accountability slide**, not a financial table. It provides **directional confirmation** (GP trough Dec/Jan, recovery Feb–Mar, KZN OP positive in final three months, UK disposal post-period) but **no hard numbers**. All numeric verification must be sourced from the income statement, debtors note, cash-flow and debt notes captured earlier.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

Two footnote markers appear on this slide; both definitions are present in the captured evidence:

- **`*` on "2nd largest food retailer*"** `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 42]` — footnote text: "* By retail sales". This qualifies the ranking claim as being measured on **retail sales**, not wholesale/turnover. Implication: the "2nd largest" positioning is a retail-sales-basis claim and is **not** reconcilable to group revenue, merchandise sales, or market-share percentages reported elsewhere without a retail-to-wholesale conversion. Must be verified against any market-share or ranking disclosure in later sections.
- **`*` on "Convenience 38% *"** `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 42]` — footnote text: "*AC Nielsen". This qualifies the 38% convenience market-share figure as an **AC Nielsen estimate**, i.e., third-party modelled data, not company-reported. Implication: treat as external estimate; not a forecast input unless corroborated.
- **`*` on "~EUR 70m EBITDA*"** `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 42]` — footnote text: "*12 months to March 2026". This is the most consequential qualification: the ~EUR 70m EBITDA is an **LTM (12 months to March 2026)** figure, not an H1 or annualised figure, and is stated in **EUR**. Implication: it cannot be directly compared to the ZAR "EBITDA pre IFRS 16 R976.4m" cited on p.31 without an FX conversion and a period-basis alignment (LTM vs H1 annualised). This directly bears on the leverage-ratio EBITDA definition questions (Q239, Q102, Q87) and must be reconciled in the debt/leverage note.

No other footnote markers or small-print qualifications are visible in the captured evidence. The tagline "We are fixing what went wrong. We are not changing what makes us different." is qualitative only.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

No footnote markers (`[^1]`, `*`, etc.) appear on p. 46. The page consists of four small-print qualifications, each of which changes how headline numbers elsewhere must be read:

1. **Forward-looking statements** `[unmapped, p. 46]`: "based on management's current expectations and projections. Actual results may differ materially. SPAR undertakes no obligation to revise or update." — Implication: **all guidance referenced in Q55/Q318/Q319 (GP%, OP margin, store openings, capex, DPS/payout, leverage) is non-binding and un-updated**; the forecast model must treat any H2/FY2027 targets as management aspiration, not commitment, and must not assume the company will refresh them intra-year.

2. **Currency** `[unmapped, p. 46]`: "All values in South African Rand (R) unless otherwise stated. **Ireland results shown in EUR for operational comparability.**" — Implication: Ireland figures (capex €15m p. 33; retailer contributions EUR3.8m; dividend €8.5m p. 31; EBITDA ~EUR70m p. 42) are **EUR-denominated and must be translated at a disclosed rate** before consolidating into the ZAR forecast. This directly bears on **Q283, Q323, Q324, Q237, Q265** — the EUR/ZAR rate used is still not disclosed here and must be located in the financial statements/segment note.

3. **Not investment advice / information purposes only** `[unmapped, p. 46]`: standard legal boilerplate; no accounting effect.

4. **Comparable basis** `[unmapped, p. 46]`: "All comparatives are restated to the **26-week calendar basis adopted in FY2025**. **Switzerland and UK operations are classified as discontinued (IFRS 5) and excluded from continuing operations in both periods shown.**" — This is the most consequential qualification on the page. It (a) confirms the 26-week comparable basis (Q1/Q205), and (b) fixes the **continuing-operations perimeter as SA + Ireland with Switzerland and UK as IFRS 5 discontinued in both periods** (Q200/Q337). Critically, **Poland is not named**, so the Poland classification (continuing vs discontinued, and whether its earnings sit in HEPS) is unresolved and must be verified in the segment/income-statement note. It also means every "continuing operations" figure used in the forecast (revenue, EBITDA R976.4m p. 31, FCF −R2.0bn p. 31, leverage) is on an **SA + Ireland only** basis, and the UK/Swiss cash flows and lease liabilities (Q272, Q291, Q242) sit outside that perimeter.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **No footnote markers (`[^1]`, `*`, etc.) are visible on p. 48.** The page carries only the appendix title "Appendix 1 | Southern Africa income statement" and the footer "INTERIM RESULTS FY2026 … 48". No small-print definitions, no `[^R]` marker, no glossary. **Verification question raised:** confirm in later appendix pages whether Appendix 1 carries footnotes that were cropped, and whether the "pre IFRS 16" EBITDA basis is defined anywhere (carry Q267/Q285/Q306/Q348).

- **"EBITDA (pre IFRS 16)" line** `[unmapped, p. 48]`: This is the first explicit appearance of a pre-IFRS 16 EBITDA figure tied to a named segment. It matters because:
  - It is the likely denominator for the SA 2.73x leverage ratio (p. 28), but on an **H1 (26-week) basis**, not LTM. If used unannualised, 2.73x would imply net debt ≈ R1,904m, which is inconsistent with SA gross debt R8,408.2m — so the leverage ratio must use an **annualised or LTM** EBITDA. This is a material reconciliation gap (carry Q239/Q260).
  - It sits **below** the PAT line in the statement, i.e., it is a non-IFRS memo line, not an IFRS subtotal. Confirm it is computed as OP before extraordinary + D&A (pre-IFRS 16), and whether it excludes or includes the R159.2m extraordinary items.

- **"Revenue other + Other income" R887.644m (+54.0%)** `[unmapped, p. 48]`: This line **bundles** other revenue and other income. Commentary says it was "lifted by the value-added services platform and the G&L liquor business." Implication: the +R311.4m jump is **not** pure merchandise/financial-services revenue — it likely includes one-off or non-recurring other income. This directly affects the revenue decomposition (Q2/Q127) and the operating-profit bridge (Q126): a large part of the OP decline offset is this other-income line, which may not be sustainable into H2. **Verification:** split "other revenue" (financial services: finance charges, initiation fees, monthly service fees, credit life) from "other income" (sundry, insurance recoveries, etc.) in the Appendices/segment note.

- **Extraordinary items R159.153m vs R79.542m (+100.1%)** `[unmapped, p. 48]`: SA extraordinary items **doubled**. Combined with the commentary that ECL/write-offs/provisions include "additional provisions of R273m (mainly KZN and SR) and R58m of write-offs in G&L," there is a **classification tension**: are the R273m/R58m credit charges inside "extraordinary items" (R159.2m) or inside "net operating expenses" (R5,334.4m, +18.5%)? The R159.2m extraordinary line is **smaller** than the R273m+R58m credit top-up, implying the credit charges sit in **operating expenses**, not extraordinary items — which would mean the "underlying" OP of R396.4m is **not** clean of the one-off credit top-up. This is a critical forecast issue: the R396.4m "before extraordinary items" OP still absorbs ~R331m of one-off credit charges. **Verification:** locate the extraordinary-items note and the opex note to confirm where the R273m/R58m sit (carry Q100/Q131/Q222).

- **Taxation −R2.400m on a pre-tax loss of −R50.864m** `[unmapped, p. 48]`: Implied ETR ≈ 4.7%, versus 26.1% prior year. A near-zero tax charge on a loss suggests **deferred tax not recognised on losses**, an **assessed-loss credit**, or a **one-off tax item**. This distorts the PAT comparison (−111.2%) and the effective-tax-rate bridge (Q132/Q199). **Verification:** tax note in Appendices.

- **"Softer dropshipment volumes and weaker case movement across G&L"** `[unmapped, p. 48]`: This is a **volume** driver, not price. It implies SA merchandise revenue growth of +1.7% was **volume-negative, price/inflation-positive**. For the forecast, this means the +1.7% topline is not a volume recovery — it is inflation/mix. **Verification:** internal inflation rate (+2.6% cited earlier) vs +1.7% revenue growth implies **negative real volume**; confirm in the revenue/volume commentary.

- **"Build it faced construction sector pressure and adverse weather, with lower consumer loyalty"** `[unmapped, p. 48]`: First explicit link between **consumer loyalty** and a specific brand (Build it). Ties to the 78.5% loyalty / 77.90% ex-KZN metric (Q49/Q110/Q150). **Verification:** confirm whether Build it loyalty is below group and whether it is inside the satisfactory-paid/collection metrics.

- **"Health delivered a strong performance"** `[unmapped, p. 48]`: Qualitative only — no revenue/GP quantification. **Verification:** Health segment revenue/GP and store count (Q90/Q184) in segment note.

- **"Higher warehousing and distribution to support KZN deliveries"** `[unmapped, p. 48]`: Confirms the KZN logistics cost step-up is **inside net operating expenses** (+18.5%), consistent with the p. 37 commentary on owned fleet vs 3PL. **Verification:** quantify KZN W&D cost increase and capex (Q301/Q307) and confirm whether it is permanent opex or capitalised.

- **"Additional IT and consultancy spend"** `[unmapped, p. 48]`: Ties to SAP/Omni strategic capex (Q281) but here described as **opex** ("IT and consultancy spend"), not capex. **Verification:** confirm split of SAP/Omni between capitalised (R191m, 29% of R659m) and expensed — a key H2 opex headwind.

- **"Stepped-up marketing campaigns"** `[unmapped, p. 48]`: Opex driver; confirm whether marketing is above or below the line and whether it reverses in H2.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **No footnote markers present** `[unmapped, p. 49]`: Appendix 2 contains no `[^1]`, `*`, or note-reference markers in the captured text. There is therefore no missing footnote text to flag for this section — but also **no definitions** for the two qualified line items below, which must be verified in later appendices.

- **"EBITDA (pre IFRS 16)" EUR 29,773k** `[unmapped, p. 49]`: Presented as a memorandum line below PAT, with no reconciliation to operating profit and no definition. It is a **half-year** figure. Implication: to use in the group leverage build-up (Ireland 3.29x per p. 28), we need (a) the EUR→ZAR rate, (b) confirmation of LTM vs H1-annualised basis, and (c) confirmation that "pre IFRS 16" excludes lease depreciation and lease interest consistently with the SA R697.408m figure (p. 48). Arithmetic check: Ireland EBITDA pre IFRS 16 EUR 29,773k vs operating profit EUR 25,286k implies ~EUR 4,487k of add-backs (D&A ex-ROU plus lease adjustments) — **not** reconcilable from this section alone.

- **"Extraordinary items" EUR 403k vs EUR 159k (+153.5%)** `[unmapped, p. 49]`: Sits **below** "Operating profit before extraordinary items" and **above** "Operating profit." Implication: Ireland's headline operating profit (EUR 25,286k) includes a EUR 403k extraordinary credit/gain; the "before extraordinary" margin (2.9%) is the cleaner recurring measure. The nature of the EUR 403k is **not disclosed** here — must be verified in the extraordinary-items note (ties to Q19/Q361 for SA; Ireland equivalent open).

- **Accounting-estimate change qualification** `[unmapped, p. 49]`: Commentary states "admin, IT and depreciation reflect a change in accounting estimates (YTD depreciation catch-up in Nov 2025) and timing on RCC amortisation in Dec 2025." Implication: part of the +4.7% net operating expense growth is a **one-off catch-up** (depreciation) and a **timing shift** (RCC amortisation), not underlying cost inflation. This means the underlying Ireland opex growth is **lower** than 4.7%, and H2 2026 opex should **not** annualise the H1 catch-up. Must be quantified in the Ireland opex/PP&E note.

- **"UK operations are treated as discontinued"** `[unmapped, p. 49]`: Confirms the Ireland statement is **continuing operations only** (UK excluded). Implication: Ireland EBITDA/OP here is the correct continuing-ops base for group build-up; UK losses sit in discontinued operations and must be excluded from continuing-ops margin and FCF (ties to Q272, Q343).

- **Revenue/GP qualification** `[unmapped, p. 49]`: Commentary attributes +2.2% revenue to a strong start then a challenging Feb/March (severe weather, sentiment at three-year low), softer tobacco volumes (minimal margin impact), and expected further rate rises/food inflation. GP% +20bps driven by vaping regulatory switch (single-use → longer-life, higher wholesale margin), alcohol promotions/RTD shift, and favourable tobacco mix. Implication: the GP% uplift is **mix-driven and partly regulatory one-off** (vaping switch) — sustainability into H2 must be tested; tobacco volume decline is a **revenue headwind with minimal margin impact**, so revenue growth overstates underlying volume.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **No footnote markers (`[^1]`, `*`, etc.) are present on p. 50.** The only small-print qualifications are parenthetical period comparators:
  - **"(Sep 2025: 11)"** and **"(Sep 2025: 17)"** for corporate stores / independent retailers `[unmapped, p. 50]`.
  - **"(Mar 2025: 10)"** for independent-retailer establishment count `[unmapped, p. 50]`.
  - **Implication**: These confirm the JV's **September financial year-end**, meaning the "H1 2026" column is **Oct 2025–Mar 2026**, not the group's 26 weeks to late-March. Any consolidation of this JV into group continuing operations therefore involves a **calendar mismatch** that must be verified (new Q386).
  - **Store-count movement unpacked**: corporate stores **11 → 12 (+1)**; independent retailers **17 → 13 (−4)**. The commentary attributes slower-than-planned store openings and higher establishment costs to **independent-retailer establishment** (Mar 2025: 10), yet the independent-retailer count **fell by 4** — a tension between "independent retailer growth" narrative and the disclosed count. This is a verification trigger (new Q387).
  - **Margin/opex unpacked**: GM% fell 19.7% → 19.4% (−30bps) while revenue grew +7.6%; GP grew only +5.9%, so **cost of sales grew faster than sales** (~+8.0% implied). Operating profit fell −71.5% on establishment expenses +14.0%, S&D +7.3%, personnel +12.2% — i.e. **opex growth (~+10–12%) far outpaced GP growth (+5.9%)**, the core driver of the OP collapse. No quantification of each line in Rand/Rs is given beyond the % changes — see new Q388.
  - **No definition** of "establishment expenses," "sales and distribution," or "personnel costs" is provided; no IFRS 16/pre-IFRS 16 distinction; no indication whether the JV is equity-accounted or consolidated. These remain open (Q385–Q389).

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **No footnote markers (`[^1]`, `*`, `[^R]`) are visible on p.53.** The page is a strategic-priorities divider with KPI callouts only. There is therefore no footnote text to unpack, and no missing-footnote flag is required — but this should be re-verified on re-capture (see Q400 below).
- **KPI callout qualification — "Project 125 – Doubling the Pharmacy Network"**: The headline numbers **47 pharmacies signed**, **28 pharmacies launched**, **65%+ loyalty (P125 stores)**, **+27%+ wholesale purchases growth** are presented without definitions. Critical ambiguities:
  1. **"Signed" vs "launched"**: 47 signed but only 28 launched implies a 19-store launch pipeline; the 65%+ loyalty and +27%+ wholesale growth targets appear to attach to **P125 stores** (i.e., the launched cohort), not the signed cohort — must be confirmed.
  2. **"Doubling the Pharmacy Network"**: base network size is not stated on this page; cannot verify whether 47 signed ≈ doubling, or whether 28 launched is the relevant doubling metric. Ties to Q184 (+19 net openings) and Q5/Q119/Q140 store counts.
  3. **"+27%+ wholesale purchases growth"**: base period, whether like-for-like or including new stores, and whether this is a target or achieved metric are all undefined. This is a **revenue-driver** for the Health wholesale line and must be reconciled to reported Health revenue in the segment note.
  4. **"65%+ loyalty"**: undefined — is this the same loyalty metric as the group 78.5% G&L satisfactory-paid proxy (Q49/Q110/Q150), or a Health-specific loyalty-programme participation rate? If the latter, it must **not** be conflated with the credit-book satisfactory-paid metric.
- **Six numbered priorities (1 Profitability recovery; 2 Aptekor scale-up; 3 KZN wholesaler license; 4 Academy enrolment recovery; 5 Pharmacy Guild & network defence; 6 SPAR Rewards in pharmacies)** are named but **entirely unquantified** — no capex, opex, revenue, or EBITDA impact. These are forward-looking claims requiring financial verification in the Health segment note / capex section.
- **"KZN wholesaler license"** is a potentially material structural item (vertical integration into wholesale) that could shift revenue recognition (wholesale vs retail) and gross margin mix — must be checked against the segment/accounting-policy note.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **Footnote block on p.55 (three definitions, `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 55]`)**:
  - "ROIC - Pre-IFRS 16 Net operating profit after tax (NOPAT) divided by Invested capital (average debt plus average shareholders equity)"
  - "ROE - Pre-IFRS 16 Profit after tax (PAT) divided by average shareholders equity"
  - "ROCE - Pre-IFRS 16 Net operating profit divided by capital employed (average total assets less average current liabilities)"
  - **What it changes**: All three return metrics are struck **pre-IFRS 16**, so the "average debt" in invested capital and the "net operating profit" in the numerator **exclude lease liabilities and lease finance/depreciation**. This means the reported ROIC 8.3% / ROCE 11.7% / ROE 7.8% are **not directly comparable** to a post-IFRS 16 return on capital, and the "average debt" base is inconsistent with the balance-sheet presentation where lease liabilities R8,420.2m sit separately from borrowings R8,408.2m (p.27). It also confirms the group's convention of quoting returns and leverage on a pre-IFRS 16 basis — which must be carried consistently into the forecast (i.e., do not add lease liabilities to the debt base when testing the 2.73x/3.29x/2.12x leverage ratios).
  - **What must be verified later**: (i) whether "average debt" is gross borrowings or net debt; (ii) whether "average shareholders equity" is group or entity; (iii) whether NOPAT uses the statutory or adjusted tax rate (given SA ETR ≈4.7% p.48 and Ireland ≈16.6% p.49); (iv) whether the same pre-IFRS 16 convention applies to the leverage ratios on p.28.

- **Chart data labels (`[unmapped, p. 55]`)** — the bar chart shows **ROIC / ROE / ROCE** for Southern Africa, Ireland and Group. The captured labels are: **17.4%** (Ireland, ROCE), **14.1%** (Ireland, ROE), **11.7%** (Group, ROCE), **8.3%** (Group, ROIC), **7.8%** (Group, ROE), **6.5%** (Southern Africa, ROCE), **3.7%** (Southern Africa, ROIC), and **−6.8%** (Southern Africa, ROE). The capture is **partially garbled** — the mapping of each label to its bar/series is not fully legible, and one Southern Africa series (ROE) appears as **−6.8%**, which is a material negative return that is **not explained in the commentary**. This is a significant anomaly: the commentary says "Strong returns across all metrics; ROCE 17.4% reflects high capital efficiency" (Ireland) and "ROIC 3.7% and ROCE 6.5% reflect H1 margin compression" (SA), but does **not** mention a **negative SA ROE of −6.8%**. That negative ROE implies SA PAT is negative (loss-making) on an average-equity base — consistent with the SA OP margin of 0.5% (p.48) and net finance costs, but it must be reconciled to the reported SA profit line. **Verification required**: confirm the −6.8% label attaches to SA ROE (not another series), and reconcile to SA PAT.

- **No footnote markers (`[^1]`, `*`, `[^R]`) are visible on p.55** — the only small-print is the three-definition block above. The `[^R]` marker (p.32) and FCF/comparable-basis/retailer-contribution definitions remain unlocated.

- **Capture warning**: "The boundary crosses text. Enlarge the area to include full characters, headings and footnotes." The chart labels and the mapping of each % to its series are therefore **unreliable**; the numbers above should be treated as provisional until re-captured.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **No footnote markers (`[^1]`, `*`, `[^R]`) are present on p.57.** The page is a clean strategy slide with no small-print definitions. This is itself a finding: the SAP appendix does **not** define "capex budget," "payback," "ring-fenced," or "finance foundation stable," all of which are load-bearing for the forecast.

- **Qualification 1 — "Total capex budget unchanged" / "No increase in capex — sequenced for payback"** `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 57]`.
  - **What it changes**: This is a **capex-envelope constraint**. It implies the SAP programme (Finance Go-Live FY2026, DC Integration FY2027) is funded **within** the existing R659m gross / R438.7m net capex envelope (pp.31/33), not additive. For the forecast this means: (a) H2 FY2026 capex should not be grossed up for SAP; (b) the R191m capitalised SAP figure (29% of R659m, p.33) is the ceiling, not a floor; (c) any SAP overrun must be offset elsewhere in the capex budget — a risk to store refurbishment or fleet capex (Q301). **Must verify**: the actual SAP capitalised amount and whether "unchanged" is measured gross or net of retailer contributions (Q263).

- **Qualification 2 — "DC integration follows in FY2027 only once the finance foundation is confirmed stable" / "The highest-risk phase… does not begin until controls are proven"** `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 57]`.
  - **What it changes**: This is a **phasing and contingency qualification**. It pushes the highest-risk SAP phase (DC integration, touching retailer ordering and fulfilment) into **FY2027**, i.e. beyond the H2 FY2026 forecast horizon. For the forecast: (a) H2 FY2026 should carry **no DC-integration disruption cost or benefit**; (b) FY2027 carries the disruption risk and the payback; (c) the "confirmed stable" gate is an **unquantified contingency** — if the finance foundation slips, DC integration slips, and the FY2027 benefit is deferred. **Must verify**: whether any FY2027 guidance (p.9/p.40) already assumes DC-integration benefit, and whether a slip contingency is disclosed.

- **Qualification 3 — "The management reporting gap that allowed KZN to deteriorate undetected is structurally closed — earlier visibility, earlier intervention"** `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 57]`.
  - **What it changes**: This is a **root-cause remediation claim** that reframes the KZN issue (Q369) as a **reporting/controls failure**, not a pure cost event. For the forecast: (a) it supports the assumption that the KZN W&D cost increase is **non-recurring in cause** (controls fixed) even if the cost base is permanent; (b) it implies **no further "undetected" deterioration** of the same type — a forecast risk-reducer; (c) it does **not** quantify the KZN cost or its reversal. **Must verify**: the KZN W&D cost quantum (Q369) and whether "structurally closed" is audited/assured or management assertion only.

- **Qualification 4 — "Real-time data… will support real-time tracking of margin recovery initiatives"** `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 57]`.
  - **What it changes**: This is a **forward-looking capability claim** tied to the margin-recovery narrative (Q423). ### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **No footnote markers on p. 58.** Appendix 11 `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 58]` contains **no `[^1]`, `*`, or note references** and **no small-print definitions**. The slide is a pure infographic/table of Ireland (BWG) market-position KPIs. This is a **negative finding** relevant to Q384/Q397/Q416/Q422/Q438: the glossary/definitions appendix is **not** App 11.

- **KPI qualifications embedded in the table (unqualified, must be verified):**
  - **"1,068 Stores across Ireland"** — no split between company-owned (CoCo) and franchise, no net openings/closures, no trading space m², no trading density. Must be reconciled to the Ireland segment note (Q374/Q376) and to the 127 retail properties (102 franchise / 25 CoCo) — note the **1,068 stores vs 127 retail properties** gap implies the vast majority of the 1,068 are independently owned franchise/retailer stores supplied via the voluntary trading model, not group-owned properties. This distinction matters for **revenue recognition (wholesale vs retail), GP% mix, and IFRS 16 lease exposure**.
  - **"2,142 People employed"** — "Across all operations"; no split of group vs franchise; must be tied to Ireland personnel cost line (Q383).
  - **"20 Cash & Carrys — Value Centre network"** — wholesale channel; must be reconciled to Ireland wholesale vs retail revenue split (Q382) and to the "9% foodservice wholesale share."
  - **"127 Retail properties — 102 franchise / 25 CoCo"** — the only owned/leased property disclosure on the slide; must be tied to Ireland IFRS 16 ROU assets, lease liabilities and depreciation (Q376/Q377).
  - **"9% Foodservice wholesale share — Growing channel"** — no base period, no growth rate; must be quantified against Ireland revenue (Q378/Q382).
  - **"98.5% Service level — Consistent supplier fill"** — operational KPI; no financial linkage disclosed; check whether it ties to any service-level penalty/rebate in the Ireland GP bridge (Q378).
  - **"80% BWG Foodservice growth Since 2021"** — cumulative vs CAGR undefined; must be verified and tied to foodservice revenue line (Q382).
  - **"1m+ Shoppers every day"** and **"38% Largest convenience market share"** — market-share base (Ireland convenience market size, value vs volume) undefined; must be verified against any external/market data cited in the segment note.
  - **"#1 Irish Voluntary Trading Group By store count"** — ranking basis (store count only) stated; no revenue ranking; must be confirmed.

- **What this changes for the forecast:** p. 58 supplies the **Ireland operating footprint** (1,068 stores; 20 Cash & Carry; 127 retail properties 102 franchise/25 CoCo; 2,142 employees) that must anchor the Ireland revenue, GP%, opex, IFRS 16 and leverage build. It does **not** supply any P&L, balance-sheet, cash-flow, FX or ratio figures — so the Ireland EBITDA EUR 29,773k, leverage 3.29x, ROIC/ROE/ROCE and the EUR→ZAR translation all remain to be verified in the Ireland segment/financial note and FX note.
